extra.why_retire_not_hold: Considered and rejected treating the ~$55/month statistical-upper-bound caveat as grounds for a time-boxed hold. Two reasons it does not: precondition #4 is a deterministic governance FAIL independent of any amount of additional tape (validation.json extra.recommendation says this outright), so a hold would sit waiting on an approval decision this record cannot itself produce or accelerate; and the pre-start fee-net edge has literally never printed positive in 72,875 priced paths, so the only way to reach the $20 bar is to import a post-start-magnitude edge into a pre-start scenario that has never exhibited it — the validator's own words are that this 'should not be read as grounds for continued investment.' A hold would keep an inert record open indefinitely with no lever in this chain to resolve it; retiring it is honest about that and the collector keeps running regardless.

rationale: Validation returned go_no_go='no_go' on a clean, pre-registered primary statistic: 0/79 games with a qualifying, persistent pre-start dislocation; game-level 95% Clopper-Pearson CI [0.0%, 4.56%], one-sided upper bound 3.72% (research/validation/strat_crossvenue_mlb_v1_validation_2026-08-11.json, uncertainty + primary_statistic_detail). The zero held at every stress cell tried — 4 slippage levels, 3 thresholds, both persistence rules — and is described in the report itself as 'not a fragile result sitting near a boundary' (stress_tests.summary).

The pre-start fee-net edge was never once positive in the entire sample: median -$0.05, p95 -$0.04, max -$0.01 across 72,875 priced pre-start paths, versus a post-start max of +$0.51 (validation.json performance.net_edge_units and extra.net_edge_distribution_pre_vs_post). This is described in the spec's own null_hypothesis and fair_value_model as the exact question under test, and the tape answers it: the pregame parity relationship holds almost exactly, it is not merely under-sampled.

Entry_logic precondition #4 (settlement_equivalence.state=='verified' for gemini_kalshi_mlb_moneyline) is a hard, deterministic FAIL today — config/settlement_equivalence.yaml: decision='not_equivalent', approval=null, 4 of 8 dimensions marked 'different' (spec .../strat_crossvenue_mlb_v1_2026-08-10.json entry_logic precondition 4; validation.json extra.precondition_4_settlement_equivalence; independently re-confirmed against src/settlement_registry.py's enforcement in the integrity report). This is a governance/documentation decision, not a data question, and the validator states explicitly that 'more tape collection would not change this precondition's status' (validation.json extra.recommendation). No amount of holding resolves it without a separate, human-approved change to that config, which this record cannot itself produce.

Integrity passed on the mechanism, not the outcome: every checkable claim in the spec — the fee formulas, the settlement-equivalence state machine and its code-level enforcement, the postponement/rescheduling divergence read verbatim from both venues' pinned rule PDFs, and the matching/phase-classification logic's correct avoidance of the open-market close_time placeholder trap (CLAUDE.md) — checked out against primary sources and code (research/integrity/strat_crossvenue_mlb_v1_integrity_2026-08-10.json, status=pass, blocking_issues=[]). The integrity report itself frames this as 'a correct description of a blocked strategy,' i.e. confirmation that the spec is honest, not that the strategy has edge.

The honest statistical-upper-bound caveat (~$55/month, above the $20 capacity bar) is acknowledged but does not support a hold: it requires simultaneously assuming (a) the loosest rate statistically consistent with observing zero in 79 games, AND (b) an edge-per-path magnitude (the $0.51 max) that has never once been observed pre-start — it is borrowed from the post-start regime because pre-start 'never had a positive value to draw from' (validation.json capacity.upper_bound_statistical_scenario.scenario_edge_source). The validator's own recommendation, reached before this review, is 'not worth pursuing settlement-equivalence review on the strength of this evidence' (validation.json extra.recommendation) — this decision adopts that conclusion rather than overriding it.

Holding this record open would not accelerate a legitimate advance: this spec's own gate_this_feeds note states it 'proposes no independent live forward gate' and exists only to inform whether settlement-equivalence review is worth pursuing at all (spec .../strat_crossvenue_mlb_v1_2026-08-10.json extra.validation_guidance.gate_this_feeds) — and the validator already answered that question 'no'. Continuing to hold a record whose only open question is a governance approval that nothing in this chain can grant serves no research purpose and risks being mistaken for an active line of work.
required_conditions: A successor variant is worth opening as a NEW opportunity/spec (never a re-spec of this retired record — the registry forbids that, by design) only if BOTH of the following hold, not either alone:

(1) config/settlement_equivalence.yaml records decision='verified' for gemini_kalshi_mlb_moneyline via a reviewed, versioned change carrying an approval.approved_by and approval.approved_at and all 8 dimensions marked 'equivalent' (per src/settlement_registry.py's own enforcement, confirmed live in the integrity report) — not merely a documentation edit asserting equivalence, and not inferred from schedule coverage or any other proxy.

(2) The ongoing (collector-continued) tape shows actual pre-start qualifying, persistent dislocations materializing at a rate and magnitude that clear the $20/month economic bar as a POINT ESTIMATE, not merely as an unexcluded statistical upper bound borrowed from a different market phase — i.e., at least a handful of qualifying persistent pre-start episodes observed directly, at pre-start-observed edge magnitudes (not the post-start $0.51 tail), across a materially larger sample than 79 games.

If only (1) clears (equivalence approved) but the tape still shows zero pre-start qualifying episodes, or only (2)-style loose statistical bounds without direct observation, that is not sufficient grounds to reopen this line — file it as a new card with the updated evidence and let the chain re-run from opportunity_registered.
